overview: Student Geto’s settings tune summon placement, energy gain, three cursed-energy barrage stages, and the cameras used during them.
technicalOverview: Suguru Geto (Student) (CP_121) uses UCP_121_ActionController with a behaviour-controller shell and character-specific action templates. Normal attacks dismiss and resummon shikigami 0 through CN_180; cursed-energy attacks summon, hold and release shikigami 1 through CN_200. Nine ordered CharacterUniqueDataTable4 rows become optional row pointers read through an unchecked UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] accessor. They tune shared gain/effect values, normal-attack placement, three cursed-energy-1 barrage stages, their mode-2 cameras, and the cursed-energy-2 summon/drain. This describes reconstructed consumer code: verified means the reader and downstream effect are traced; observed would mean only forwarding is traced.

CP_121.title: Shared character and effect-base values
CP_121.overview: Base row for gain multipliers, shikigami-0 hit-effect offsets, discarded early-finish reads, and delayed-effect clearance.

0.label: Level 1 attack energy-gain multiplier
0.simple: Level 1 attacks give 3x the damage row’s cursed-energy gain.
0.technical: GetAttackCursedEnergyGainRate returns this only when CursedEnergyLevel == 1; the status controller multiplies it by DamageRow->CursedEnergy_Add_Attacker and adds it to cursed energy. Same-team receivers are skipped.

1.label: Level 2 attack energy-gain multiplier
1.simple: Level 2 attacks give 4x the damage row’s cursed-energy gain.
1.technical: Same slot-117 path, selected when CursedEnergyLevel == 2. Levels outside 1..3 return 1.0 without reading a unique index.

2.label: Level 3 attack energy-gain multiplier
2.simple: Level 3 attacks give 5x the damage row’s cursed-energy gain.
2.technical: Same slot-117 path, selected when CursedEnergyLevel == 3.

3.label: First normal-hit effect offset X
3.simple: The first normal-attack summon effect sits 45 units behind the summon point.
3.technical: TCP_121_NormalAttack_1_1 phase 0 passes FVector(U3,U4,U5) to SpawnAttackEffect with the shikigami transform and scale 0.25; the helper rotates the components by the transform axes, adds them to the translation, and spawns FX_CP_121_00111. X is -45 world units on the forward axis.

4.label: First normal-hit effect offset Y
4.simple: The first effect has no right-axis offset.
4.technical: Y component of the same SpawnAttackEffect offset vector; 0 world units on the right axis.

5.label: First normal-hit effect offset Z
5.simple: The first effect has no up-axis offset.
5.technical: Z component of the same SpawnAttackEffect offset vector; 0 world units on the up axis.

6.label: Normal Attack 2 shikigami effect offset X
6.simple: The Attack_2 hit effect is offset 1 unit along the shikigami forward axis.
6.technical: The _2 branch sets AttackRequest.Vector70 = FVector(U6,U7,U8) and orders Attack_2; FCN_180_Attack_2::Start forwards that vector to SpawnAttackEffect as the FX_CP_121_00111 offset.

7.label: Normal Attack 2 shikigami effect offset Y
7.simple: The Attack_2 effect has no right-axis offset.
7.technical: Y component of the Attack_2 Vector70 forwarded to the shikigami effect.

8.label: Normal Attack 2 shikigami effect offset Z
8.simple: The Attack_2 effect has no up-axis offset.
8.technical: Z component of the Attack_2 Vector70 forwarded to the shikigami effect.

9.label: Normal Attack 3 shikigami effect offset X
9.simple: The Attack_3 hit effect is offset 68 units behind the shikigami.
9.technical: The _3 branch sets AttackRequest.Vector70 = FVector(U9,U10,U11) and orders Attack_3, whose Start forwards it to SpawnAttackEffect. Separately, NormalAttack_1_1::FinishAttackEffects reads 11,10,9 and discards them before finishing the shikigami effect.

10.label: Normal Attack 3 shikigami effect offset Y
10.simple: The Attack_3 effect has no right-axis offset.
10.technical: Y component of the Attack_3 Vector70 consumed by the shikigami effect; also read and discarded in the early-finish path.

11.label: Normal Attack 3 shikigami effect offset Z
11.simple: The Attack_3 effect has no up-axis offset.
11.technical: Z component of the Attack_3 Vector70 consumed by the shikigami effect; also read and discarded in the early-finish path. Zero itself is not evidence of disuse.

12.label: Delayed-effect forward clearance
12.simple: Delayed effects check up to 150 units forward for blockers.
12.technical: AddDelayedDetachEffect builds Extent = FVector(U12,U13,50) for StateCondition_ClampLocalOffset. The helper traces toward Offset.X - Extent.X and reduces Offset.X from the first filtered hit distance; world units.

13.label: Delayed-effect side clearance
13.simple: Delayed effects check up to 50 units sideways for blockers.
13.technical: Y component of the clamp Extent; the helper traces along the right axis chosen by sign(Offset.Y) and rewrites Offset.Y. The Z extent is hard-coded 50 and is not read from this row.

notes.text: The discarded reads at indices 9-11 are real but write no state in FinishAttackEffects; they are retained because the same floats are used by Attack_3.

CP_121_NORMALATTACK.title: Normal attack shikigami placement and timing
CP_121_NORMALATTACK.overview: Repeated dismissal/resummon of shikigami 0: the first hit places a copy around the owner, later hits resummon it at the target, and Attack_2/Attack_3 reposition it with attack parameters.

0.label: First resummon delay
0.simple: The dismissed shikigami returns after 0.75 seconds.
0.technical: Phase 1 increments ActionElapsedTime and returns while U0 > ActionElapsedTime (strict); at or after 0.75 it activates shikigami 0 and orders Attack_1. Seconds.

1.label: Attack_1 release delay
1.simple: The summoned shikigami waits at least 1 second before asking to be released.
1.technical: Copied into FShikigamiDamageActionParam.Value64 for Attack_1. FCN_180_Attack_1::Tick returns before requesting release while its Elapsed is below that value. Seconds.

2.label: First placement forward offset
2.simple: The first summoned copy starts 20 units behind the owner.
2.technical: Phase 0 computes Location = owner location + facing*U2 + right*U3 + up*U4, then aims at the secondary target or straight ahead. Value -20 world units.

3.label: First placement right offset
3.simple: The copy is placed 150 units to the owner’s right.
3.technical: Y/right component of the same placement vector; world units.

4.label: First placement up offset
4.simple: The copy is placed 115 units above the owner.
4.technical: Z/up component of the same placement vector; world units.

5.label: First placement pitch limit
5.simple: The first copy aims at most 20 degrees up or down.
5.technical: Stored as PitchLimit and passed as both MaxUp and MaxDown to CN122_AimRotation, whose elevation clamp uses degree limits.

6.label: First placement yaw limit
6.simple: The first copy aims at most 20 degrees sideways.
6.technical: Stored as YawLimit and passed as MaxYaw to CN122_AimRotation; its yaw is capped in degrees and the sign comes from the target side.

7.label: Attack_2 placement drop
7.simple: The later copy is placed 500 units lower before ground clamping.
7.technical: The Normal Attack 2 branch lowers the target-relative location by FVector::UpVector * U7, then snaps it up if ground is higher. World units.

8.label: Attack_2 target lead distance
8.simple: The copy is pushed 350 units along the target’s movement direction when possible.
8.technical: Distance starts as U8, becomes 0 if the secondary target is in action slot 146, and is quartered if MoveDelta3D0 is zero. If still positive, a line trace runs that far forward and uses the first hit X/Y, or the location moves by direction * Distance. World units.

9.label: Attack_3 placement scale
9.simple: The target-relative Attack_3 offset is multiplied by 50.
9.technical: In the _3 branch, Offset = Direction.RotateAngleAxis(U10, Direction ^ Up) and Location = secondary target location + Offset * U9 when valid, else owner location + facing * 1000. This is a distance multiplier, not time or degrees.

10.label: Attack_3 placement angle
10.simple: The Attack_3 approach direction is rotated 60 degrees about its horizontal normal.
10.technical: U10 is the angle passed to RotateAngleAxis for the placement direction. Degrees.

notes.text: Indices 11-13 are zero; no CP_121 character reader was identified after checking the controller, actions, shared camera helper and AI code. Other characters’ row-1 readers were not assigned.

CP_121_ATTACKG_1.title: Cursed-energy level 1 volley (stage row 2)
CP_121_ATTACKG_1.overview: CE level 1 reads stage row 2: 6 charges, wide jitter and a 400-unit aim tube.

0.label: Barrage charge count
0.simple: 6 charge effects are created before the volley can fire.
0.technical: Cast to int and stored as FEffectVolley::EffectCount. State 0 spawns one charge each spawn-window step and moves to state 1 when Count >= EffectCount - 1. Value here is 6.

1.label: Charge spawn window
1.technical: Stored as SpawnWindowDuration. State 0 uses Interval = SpawnWindowDuration / EffectCount; its delta is DeltaTime divided by owner CustomTimeDilation when positive. Value 0.15 seconds.

2.label: Fire group count
2.simple: The charges are split into 1 firing group.
2.technical: Cast to int and stored as FireGroupCount. PerGroup = EffectCount/max(GroupCount,1); shuffled slot modulo PerGroup plus one becomes each Order and Delay = Order*FireInterval. Later repeat delay uses EffectCount/max(GroupCount,0)*FireInterval. Value 1.

3.label: Barrage origin X / forward offset
3.simple: The barrage starts 300 units along the forward axis.
3.technical: X component of the Offset passed to AddUnknown168Entry. Entry origin is owner location + forward*X + right*Y + up*Z; the volley tick uses the same X/Y/Z in the bone frame for ring placement and aim origin. World units.

4.label: Barrage origin Y / right offset
4.simple: The barrage origin is shifted 0 units to the right.
4.technical: Y component of the same AddUnknown168Entry Offset and the bone right-axis ring component. Value 0 world units.

5.label: Barrage origin Z / up offset
5.simple: The barrage origin is 100 units above the reference position.
5.technical: Z component of the same Offset and the bone up-axis ring component. World units.

6.label: Charge ring radius
6.simple: Later charges form rings roughly 200 units from the origin.
6.technical: Charge positions use the PG_Attack_01 bone frame: counts 1-5 step 60 degrees at radius x0.75 (x1.125 for CE level 1 at counts 3 and 4), counts 6-12 step 45 degrees from -22.5 at radius x1.5, and counts 13-19 step 45 degrees at radius x1.5. This stage supplies base radius 200 world units.

7.label: Random placement scale
7.simple: Random up/side jitter is scaled by 0.35 of the ring radius.
7.technical: Range = (EffectCount >= 10 ? 0.325 : 0.75) * SpawnPatternRadius * SpawnRandomOffsetScale, with FRandRange(-Range,Range) for Up and Side. Value 0.35; zero means no random offset.

8.label: Shot interval
8.simple: Charges fire in waves 0.1 seconds apart.
8.technical: Stored as FireInterval. Each Delay = Order*FireInterval; an attached charge rearms to EffectCount/max(GroupCount,0)*FireInterval; the firing sound retries when volley Timer exceeds FireInterval. Dilation-compensated seconds.

9.label: Cursed-energy hold drain
9.simple: Holding this stage drains 250 cursed energy per second.
9.technical: CE1 phase 1 calls SetCursedEnergy(CursedEnergy - U9 * DeltaTime). Per-second drain while the hold phase runs, not a one-time cost. Stage 2 (CE level 1) uses 250.

10.label: Cursed-energy hold time
10.simple: The timed hold window ends after 0.4 seconds.
10.technical: Phase 1 checks hold <= ActionElapsedTime. At that point it continues only while the CE1 key is held and conditions permit; otherwise it sets the finish flag, detaches effects and restores camera with row 5. Value 0.4 seconds.

11.label: Delayed-detach spacing
11.simple: Queued delayed-detach effects are 0.1 seconds apart.
11.technical: On the second CE1 start, StartDelayedDetach(U11) sets Delay = queue index * Interval and detaches each effect. Queue size is 2/3/4 for levels 1/2/3. Value 0.1 seconds.

12.label: Aim-assist tube radius
12.simple: Shots turn toward the target only within 400 units of the volley axis.
12.technical: Stored as AimAssistRadius. With a valid secondary target transformed into the volley bone frame, the turn is attempted only when sqrt(Local.Y^2 + Local.Z^2) < radius (strict). Value 400 world units.

13.label: Maximum aim correction
13.simple: Each shot can turn at most 15 degrees toward the target.
13.technical: Stored as MaxAimCorrectionDegrees. Target direction must also be within 90 degrees of shot forward; applied turn is min(cap,angle), sign chosen by checking which rotation is closer. Value 15 degrees.

notes.text: Stage row 2 is chosen by GetCursedEnergyStage: CE level 1 -> stage 2; invalid level gives -1 and the accessor has no bounds check. Indices 9-11 are hold-phase reads; 0-8 and 12-13 build the volley on notify 1.

CP_121_ATTACKG_SHOOT_CAMERA_1.title: Cursed-energy 1 camera, stick direction 1
CP_121_ATTACKG_SHOOT_CAMERA_1.overview: Used when CE1 starts with left-stick direction 1 (Y <= -0.5) and when the timed hold ends: a close, high-FOV mode-2 lock-on view.

0.label: Camera offset X
0.simple: The camera sits -70 units along gaze forward from the eye base.
0.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2,5) copies index 0 into CameraOffset.X; the mode-2 update rotates that offset into gaze space before placing the camera.

1.label: Camera offset Y
1.simple: The camera is shifted -100 units along gaze right.
1.technical: Index 1 becomes CameraOffset.Y in the same mode-2 request.

2.label: Camera offset Z
2.simple: The camera is shifted -20 units along gaze up.
2.technical: Index 2 becomes CameraOffset.Z in the same mode-2 request.

3.label: Downward gaze limit
3.simple: Gaze may go at most 60 degrees below the eye line.
3.technical: Index 3 becomes LimitAngleDown; UpdateRequestCamera clamps downward gaze elevation.

4.label: Upward gaze limit
4.simple: Gaze may go at most 30 degrees above the eye line.
4.technical: Index 4 becomes LimitAngleUp; UpdateRequestCamera clamps upward gaze elevation.

5.label: Field of view
5.simple: Mode entry requests 110 degrees of FOV.
5.technical: Index 5 becomes FieldOfView. ChangeCameraMode starts FOV interpolation only when FOV > 0; zero leaves the current FOV unchanged. This row has 110.

6.label: FOV blend time
6.technical: Index 6 becomes FieldOfViewBlendTime. With FOV > 0 and this > 0, FovInterp starts with this duration; otherwise FOV snaps. This row has 0.25.

7.label: FOV easing selector
7.simple: Selector 3 chooses the FOV interpolation curve.
7.technical: Index 7 is cast to int: 0 Linear, 1 EaseIn, 2 EaseOut, 3 EaseInOut; other integers leave the default. This row has 3.

8.label: Gaze orbit yaw
8.simple: Gaze is orbited 10 degrees about the camera yaw.
8.technical: Index 8 becomes OrbitYaw; UpdateRequestCamera transforms the gaze by the orbit rotator.

9.label: Gaze orbit pitch
9.simple: Gaze is orbited 5 degrees about the camera pitch.
9.technical: Index 9 becomes OrbitPitch in the same orbit rotator.

10.label: Camera roll
10.simple: View roll is set to 5 degrees.
10.technical: Index 10 becomes Roll and is passed to SetViewTarget87 for the final view.

notes.text: MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads only indices 0-10 for mode 2. Indices 11-13 are zero here and no CP_121 reader was identified; zero is not proof of disuse elsewhere.

CP_121_ATTACKH.title: Cursed-energy 2 shikigami 1 summon and drain
CP_121_ATTACKH.overview: Controls the CN_200 shikigami used by Cursed Energy Attack 2: summon point, Attack_1 speed by energy level, natural end time, and drain while the shikigami is out.

0.label: Shikigami summon forward offset
0.simple: The shikigami is summoned directly beside the owner in the forward axis.
0.technical: TickAttack step 1 builds Offset = facing*U0 + right*U1 and passes it to FindSummonLocation with the shikigami summon placement height. Value 0 world units.

1.label: Shikigami summon right offset
1.simple: The summon point is 115 units to the owner’s right.
1.technical: Right-axis component of the same FindSummonLocation offset; world units.

2.label: Level 1 shikigami attack speed
2.simple: At level 1 the shikigami Attack_1 uses a 3000-unit speed/range parameter.
2.technical: TickAttack case 1 assigns Vector70.X = U2, orders Attack_1 with ValueA4 = level; FCN_200_AttackAAction uses Request.Vector70.X * 0.5 as the target of its 0.5-second range ease.

3.label: Level 2 shikigami attack speed
3.simple: At level 2 the shikigami Attack_1 uses 3500.
3.technical: Same level switch, case 2; reaches the CN_200 charge-range ease through Vector70.X.

4.label: Level 3 shikigami attack speed
4.simple: At level 3 the shikigami Attack_1 uses 4000.
4.technical: Same level switch, case 3; reaches the CN_200 charge-range ease through Vector70.X.

5.label: CE2 self-end time
5.simple: An unattended CE2 attack ends after 1.35 seconds.
5.technical: On action start count 0, when U5 <= Elapsed, the action sets finish flag 159, Byte16 and Phase MAX. Seconds; checked before the summon-step machine.

6.label: Shikigami-out cursed energy drain
6.simple: While shikigami 1 is out, cursed energy drains 25 per second.
6.technical: GetCursedEnergyDrainRate returns U6 only with slot-192 suppression false, no CE2 action before its flag-15A window, shikigami 1 requested active and not releasing; otherwise 0. Status tick applies positive Drain * DeltaTime.

notes.text: The shikigami’s Attack_1 and Summon actions are CN_200, not AGameShikigami using ShikigamiUniqueDataTable; CN_200 is documented as CP_121’s shikigami using CP_121 effects and a CP_121 counter damage row.

CP_121_ATTACKB_SHOOT_CAMERA.title: First normal attack camera
CP_121_ATTACKB_SHOOT_CAMERA.overview: Used on the first start of Normal Attack 1 / its air counterpart; restored to the saved mode when the attack finishes while in mode 2.

0.label: Camera offset X
0.simple: The camera sits -200 units along gaze forward from the eye base.
0.technical: MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2,8) copies index 0 into CameraOffset.X; the mode-2 update rotates that offset into gaze space before placing the camera.

1.label: Camera offset Y
1.simple: The camera is shifted -150 units along gaze right.
1.technical: Index 1 becomes CameraOffset.Y in the same mode-2 request.

2.label: Camera offset Z
2.simple: The camera is shifted 15 units along gaze up.
2.technical: Index 2 becomes CameraOffset.Z in the same mode-2 request.

3.label: Downward gaze limit
3.simple: Gaze may go at most 60 degrees below the eye line.
3.technical: Index 3 becomes LimitAngleDown; UpdateRequestCamera clamps downward gaze elevation.

4.label: Upward gaze limit
4.simple: Gaze may go at most 30 degrees above the eye line.
4.technical: Index 4 becomes LimitAngleUp; UpdateRequestCamera clamps upward gaze elevation.

5.label: Field of view
5.simple: Mode entry requests 110 degrees of FOV.
5.technical: Index 5 becomes FieldOfView. ChangeCameraMode starts FOV interpolation only when FOV > 0; zero leaves the current FOV unchanged. This row has 110.

6.label: FOV blend time
6.technical: Index 6 becomes FieldOfViewBlendTime. With FOV > 0 and this > 0, FovInterp starts with this duration; otherwise FOV snaps. This row has 0.25.

7.label: FOV easing selector
7.simple: Selector 3 chooses the FOV interpolation curve.
7.technical: Index 7 is cast to int: 0 Linear, 1 EaseIn, 2 EaseOut, 3 EaseInOut; other integers leave the default. This row has 3.

8.label: Gaze orbit yaw
8.simple: Gaze is orbited 10 degrees about the camera yaw.
8.technical: Index 8 becomes OrbitYaw; UpdateRequestCamera transforms the gaze by the orbit rotator.

9.label: Gaze orbit pitch
9.simple: Gaze is orbited 5 degrees about the camera pitch.
9.technical: Index 9 becomes OrbitPitch in the same orbit rotator.

10.label: Camera roll
10.simple: View roll is set to 5 degrees.
10.technical: Index 10 becomes Roll and is passed to SetViewTarget87 for the final view.

notes.text: The request is made only at action start count zero; the finish path restores the saved mode with 90 FOV and zero blend time.

Two shikigami are separate: shikigami 0 is the CN_180 dummy used by normal attacks; shikigami 1 is the CN_200 unit summoned by CP_121_ATTACKH. CN_180 actions also read their own CN_180 unique rows for dissolve/height; those are not CP_121 rows.

The unique row index for a CE1 barrage is the stage, not the attack-set level name: levels 1/2/3 map to rows CP_121_ATTACKG_1/_2/_3. Attack-set selection separately uses GetCursedEnergyAttackSetIndex (level minus one, or 3 on the finish target) with retail attack-set name arrays.

Direction 1 here means left-stick Y <= -0.5. It selects ATTACKG_1 attack sets and row 5 camera; other directions select ATTACKG_2 and row 6. CP_121 AI specialises only index 0x12 with FGameCharacterAIAction_CursedEnergyAttack1DownHold using stick (0,-1).

There is no CP_121-specific .inl. Unique reads use the out-of-line accessor and shared FGameCharacterAction helper; the inlined variant in GameCharacterActionInline.h is shared, not per-character. Verification notes record the retail accessor as the raw unchecked deref.

The controller overrides slots 86, 112, 113, 117, 192, 223, 256 and 290. Its factory creates twelve CP_121 action types and delegates others to base; the behaviour controller is a size-matched shell whose only override is the AI factory.

While shikigami 1 is out, recovery wait is forced to zero; with positive drain, zero cursed energy or defeat can force its release. The CN_200 verification note records the same shikigami/effect relationship.
